structured.approach: I fixed both refusal reasons. G3: claims and the output no longer quote test counts, coverage percentages or missed line numbers, because no cited item contains them. The exact figures stay in the JSON line ci.py prints for the spine's CI record, which is what task.code already does. G2: in this session I read ci.py and tests/test_overdue.py, and the test file now also appears in the tool view, so I cite it as tool:repo. The tests are unchanged from attempt 1. I re-ran /usr/bin/python3 ci.py in this session and it passed. I rewrote task.unit_tests.md in full: a table mapping each acceptance criterion to its test, the CI outcome before and after the new tests, and open questions.

claims.text: The CI coverage gate is COVERAGE_MIN = 90.0, and CI passes only when the code compiles, the tests succeed, coverage reaches the gate and there are no static issues
Before the new tests, line coverage was below the gate of 90%, because the bodies of the two new functions and the bucket_for 'return "1-30"' branch had no tests
With tests/test_overdue.py added, CI passes: the code compiles, all tests pass, both src/ap_aging files are fully covered (above the gate of 90%), and the static checks report no issues
The new tests are in tests/test_overdue.py, the file task.components BC-7 plans; feat.stories SA-6 allows a lane to add a new test file
Tests check that an invoice exactly 30 days past due is not listed and one 31 days past due is listed, with days taken from days_past_due (AC-05.1, AC-05.2, lesson L-007)

Tests check that a paid invoice (90 days) and a not-yet-due invoice are not listed, that rows have the five keys, the sort by days descending then id ascending as text (SYN-INV-002 before SYN-INV-003 at 42 days), 'unknown' risk, Decimal 980.5 quantised to 980.50, no call to bucket_for, and KeyError for a missing vendor (AC-05.3 to AC-05.10)
Tests check the CT-1 JSON: same order, CT-1 key order, days as an int, amount as a two-decimal string such as 1250.00, '[]' for an empty list, and no date field (AC-06.1 to AC-06.4)
bucket_for(1) and bucket_for(29) now cover the '1-30' branch raised as CQ-BE-3, and bucket_for(30) still returns '31-60'
Only tests/ was changed in this step; tests/test_aging.py and the source files are unchanged

open_questions: UQ-BE-1 (non-blocking, tied to TQ-9): AC-05.10 says a missing vendor raises KeyError, but the code reads vendor only for invoices it lists. A paid, not-yet-due or exactly-30-days invoice with no vendor raises nothing. Should a missing vendor raise for every invoice?
Carried unchanged (non-blocking): TQ-1, TQ-3, TQ-9, PQ-2. The tests pin today's interim designs and must change if an answer changes a [Pending] criterion.
structured.summary: The unit tests in tests/test_overdue.py cover STORY-05 overdue_with_risk (AC-05.1 to AC-05.10), STORY-06 overdue_rows_to_json (AC-06.1 to AC-06.4), and the existing aging functions, including the bucket_for '1-30' branch from CQ-BE-3. CI passes: all tests pass, both source files are fully covered (above the gate of 90%), and there are no static issues. The exact counts are in the spine's CI record. task.unit_tests.md has been rewritten without numbers that no source contains and without citations to files I had not read. One question remains open and does not block anything: UQ-BE-1, whether a missing vendor should raise KeyError for invoices that are not listed.
